title: Memory Editor
summary: Open Settings → Agent behavior → Memories → Open Memory Editor, or choose Memory Editor in Directory. Direct links use /memory-editor?key=memory.key.
html:
Memory Editor

Open Settings → Agent behavior → Memories → Open Memory Editor, or choose Memory Editor in Directory. Direct links use /memory-editor?key=memory.key.

To enable semantic selection, open Knowledge → Semantic Memory, choose Relevant memories only, and Save settings. Existing memories start indexing automatically; new and edited memories are indexed in the background too. The progress panel shows completed memories out of the current total, plus queued, processing, failed and interrupted counts. It refreshes automatically and remains available after reloading the page. The percentage measures completed memories, not elapsed time; a large memory can take longer than several small ones.

The same panel appears under Semantic retrieval in Memory Editor. A failed status offers Retry Memory indexing, which retries unfinished memories without rebuilding completed ones or retrying document jobs. Rebuild Memory index in Knowledge explicitly rebuilds every memory. Switching the embedding profile also queues replacement indexes automatically while semantic selection is enabled.

Search saved content, keys, tags, and recall summaries across the entire inventory. Filter by tag or general/project scope. Counts show matching and total memories; Load more retrieves the next page. This editor search does not change agent recall. Search matches literal substrings without case sensitivity, including decoded JSON strings. Each page uses the current inventory; concurrent edits can change later pages. If the inventory revision changes between pages, Load more restarts from the first page so a concurrent edit does not silently skip a record.

Select a memory to edit its content, tags, and recall details. Strings open as text; other JSON values open as formatted JSON. JSON supports objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null. Large integers are preserved because content travels as text and is parsed on the server. Changing the content format changes how the entered content is interpreted; it does not automatically convert the draft. Saved content must fit 1 MiB of compact UTF-8 JSON. Invalid JSON, nonfinite numbers and oversized values are rejected without replacing the existing memory.

New Memory requires a key, tags, and a recall summary. New memories default to general scope and user-provided basis. Saved keys are read-only. Existing memories without tags or recall details can keep that legacy metadata. Source information, the original creation time, and original provenance are retained; manual edits are recorded separately. Agents can continue updating manually edited memories. Editing content retains its recall summary, so update that summary when the meaning changes. Saving identical content and metadata keeps the existing revision and edit provenance.

For a project memory, choose an existing gateway and enter an absolute project folder. This binds recall to that gateway and project using the runtime's normal scope rules. An older memory may display Existing project when its original folder is unavailable. Editing its content preserves that binding. Select Change project binding and supply a gateway and folder to replace it explicitly.

Select Save or press Ctrl/Cmd+S. The editor shows unsaved changes and protects drafts when navigating away. Refresh updates the browser without discarding your draft. If an agent or another browser changes the record first, saving or deleting returns a conflict and keeps your draft. Copy any text you want to retain, then use Reload current memory to load the current revision explicitly. Delete asks for confirmation and uses the loaded revision, so it cannot remove a newer edit.

Changes become active immediately and are saved through the existing checkpoint system. The save indicator distinguishes active changes from changes saved to disk. Active tasks see updated revisions through normal recall refresh; in-flight requests and historical receipts stay unchanged. Editing does not call a model, count as agent inspection, or require final validation of memory application. If the status reports only an active change, disk durability is not yet confirmed.

The editor uses the existing Memory store, shared application theme, font settings, high-contrast appearance, and mobile browser/editor layout. It provides individual CRUD; it does not add pinning, bulk deletion, import/export, or revision restoration.

See the storage architecture and API/maintenance guide for implementation details. Editor flow diagrams explain drafts, revision conflicts and checkpoint confirmation.
